cf.title: Prevent object capture in CREATE/ALTER EXTENSION scripts

input.subject: Prevent object capture in CREATE/ALTER EXTENSION scripts

verdict_reasoning: The problem is stated and demand is shown, so levels 1a and 1b pass. Four fixable level 2 objections survived: security-1 (an ordinary role can add its own objects to a required extension and have them trusted), security-2 (a lookup path that skips the check fails silently), standards-compat-1 and standards-compat-2. None requires a different proposal, but the trust rule sits in core name resolution and needs a committer who knows that code.

brief.title: Ignore untrusted objects during name lookup in extension scripts
brief.problem: A CREATE EXTENSION or ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE script runs as the invoking role or as the bootstrap superuser, so an object another role planted in the extension's schema can capture a reference and run that role's code with elevated rights. Pinned search_path and @extschema@ qualification do not help, because the plant sits in the script's own schema. Hosted platforms that run extension scripts as superuser for users are the main case.
brief.proposed_design: While creating_extension is set, relation, type, function and operator lookups skip untrusted objects, for qualified and search_path names. An object is trusted if it is in pg_catalog, owned by a superuser or by the role running the script, or belongs to the extension or one it requires. Cached plans record whether they were analyzed in a script, and 0001 passes the script state to parallel workers.
user_visible_surface: Extension scripts that reference an object owned by another ordinary role, even schema-qualified, now fail as if the object did not exist.
New error detail saying a candidate was ignored, and a hint naming the ignored candidate when argument types do not match.
Overload resolution inside scripts can pick a different function or operator than before.
author_claims: Closes object capture through planted overloads, operators, domains and tables during script execution.
Ordinary parsing outside extension scripts is unchanged.
The trust rule accepts built-ins, the extension's own objects and required extensions' objects, so normal scripts keep working.
References to objects owned by other ordinary roles should be rare.
Complements the opt-in "extensions with an owned schema" proposal, which only helps new extensions.
brief.thread_state: Two reviewers reproduced the bug and report that v1 fixes it without finding problems; no committer has replied. The author posted v2 to also check schema-qualified relation and type names, and the CommitFest entry is in Needs review.
unclear: No number on the cost of the trust check, including the pg_depend lookup, for large extension scripts.
Which existing contrib or third-party extensions reference objects of roles outside their requires list and would now fail.
Whether operator classes, collations, text search objects, casts and conversions can still be used for capture; the author says they may have missed a route.
How the patch handles extension function bodies called after installation, beyond saying that needs another mechanism.
No documentation hunk is shown, so the change to "Security Considerations for Extension Scripts" is unknown.
Whether a trusted extension installed as bootstrap superuser treats objects owned by the installing non-superuser as trusted.
search_queries: ignore objects owned by untrusted roles

prior_attempts.title: Fix search_path for maintenance commands
prior_attempts.quote: I am withdrawing this patch from the CF until it's more clear that this is what we really want to do.
prior_attempts.reason: Jeff Davis withdrew the patch after a reviewer reported that it no longer applied to HEAD, saying it was not yet clear this was the right change. He had already noted that it forces search_path in maintenance commands but not in other contexts, and that his broader proposals to fix search_path for functions got little agreement. Earlier concerns about breaking functions that depend on search_path were raised in messages not shown. Nathan Bossart supported committing it.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P3 forced search_path to "pg_catalog, pg_temp" during maintenance commands. This proposal keeps search_path and filters candidates by owner during extension scripts, so it also blocks plants in the script's own schema.

objections.title: Membership in a required extension can be granted by an ordinary role
objections.failure_scenario: An ordinary role installs a trusted extension that another extension requires, so it owns that extension. It creates f(text) in the shared schema and runs alter extension ... add function f(text). A superuser or platform later installs the dependent extension, and its script resolves f('abc') to the planted function because it is a member of a required extension.
objections.argument: The trust rule in message #1 accepts any member of a required extension, "regardless of who owns them". alter extension add needs only ownership of the extension and of the object. A non-superuser who installs a trusted extension owns it, so membership is a property an attacker can set. The hosted-platform case the proposal targets is where unprivileged users install trusted extensions on their own.
objections.author_must_show: How does the trust rule stop an ordinary role that owns a required extension from adding its own objects to it and having them trusted?

critic.reasoning: A non-superuser who installs a trusted extension owns it, and alter extension ... add needs only ownership of the extension and of the object. The rule in message #1 trusts members of required extensions regardless of owner, and the thread does not address this route.

objections.title: Each lookup path must opt in, and a missed path fails silently
objections.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new lookup route, or changes an existing one, without calling the trust check. Scripts on that route go back to resolving planted objects. No test fails, and the gap shows up as a security report against a guarantee the project now documents.
objections.argument: The protection depends on every relevant lookup site calling the check. v1 already missed the qualified branches of RangeVarGetRelidExtended() and LookupTypeNameExtended() (message #7). Message #1 leaves operator classes, collations, text search objects, casts and conversions unfiltered and says a route may have been missed. Once the guarantee is committed, the project has to keep it complete in all of these places.
objections.author_must_show: What makes a new or changed name-lookup path fail loudly, in tests or by construction, when it skips the trust check during extension scripts?

critic.reasoning: Message #7 shows v1 missed the qualified relation and type branches after two reviews found no problem. Message #1 lists lookup paths that remain unfiltered and says a route may have been missed, and nothing shown makes a skipped check fail loudly.

objections.title: Existing scripts can stop working on update, and there is no escape hatch
objections.failure_scenario: An extension script references an object owned by an ordinary role, for example a function of a superuser=false extension that is optional or only a transitive dependency. After the server upgrade, ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE fails with "does not exist". On a hosted platform the user cannot change object ownership or edit the script, so the update stays blocked.
objections.argument: Message #1 names this behaviour change and calls such references "rare", but gives no survey of contrib or third-party scripts. The proposal has no control-file option or other way to mark an object as trusted. The only fixes are to reassign ownership to a superuser or to add a requires entry, and neither is open to the user who hits the error. The commit message carries Reported-by, so a committer would also likely ask whether this is meant for back branches.
objections.author_must_show: Which existing extension scripts reference objects of ordinary roles outside their requires list, and how does a user unblock an update when one fails?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 confirms that a schema-qualified reference to another ordinary role's object now fails, and offers only "should be rare" as evidence. The proposal names no way for a user to unblock a failed update, and the brief lists the affected extensions as unknown.

objections.title: The requires list becomes a name-visibility rule
objections.failure_scenario: Extension A requires B, and B requires C, where C is a superuser=false extension owned by an ordinary role. A's script calls a C function by its schema-qualified name. With this patch the call fails, although A installs only when C is present. The extension author finds out from a user's failed CREATE EXTENSION.
objections.argument: Today requires controls install order and @extschema:name@ substitution. Under 0002 it also decides which objects a script can see, and only for direct entries, as message #1 says. Extension authors would have to list transitive and conditional dependencies to keep scripts working. No documentation hunk is shown, so the new meaning of requires does not yet appear in the extension-authoring docs.
objections.author_must_show: Why is trust limited to direct requires entries, and where would the new meaning of requires be documented for extension authors?

critic.reasoning: Message #1 says objects of an extension outside the direct requires list are untrusted, so the A, B, C scenario follows from the stated rule. The thread gives no reason for stopping at direct entries.

refuted.title: Every current and future lookup path must remember the trust check
refuted.failure_scenario: A later patch adds a new object kind, a new lookup cache, or a new qualified-name branch in namespace.c or the parser and does not call the trust test. Extension scripts can be captured again through that path. Nobody finds out until a new security report arrives, because no test or assertion fails.
refuted.argument: The defense is spread over separate lookup routines and caches: relation, type, function and operator lookup, the operator lookaside cache, plancache and the plpgsql simple-expression path. Version 1 already missed the qualified branches for relations and types, which message #7 fixed only after review had passed. Message #1 lists paths that remain unfiltered, such as operator classes, collations, casts and text search objects, and says a route may have been missed. No committer who knows namespace.c or the parser has replied yet to take on owning this list.
refuted.author_must_show: What makes a future lookup path that skips the trust check fail loudly, in tests or by construction, so the gap does not ship unnoticed?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of security-2, which states the same scenario and the same question to the author. The remark that no committer has replied belongs in committability and does not support the verdict.

refuted.title: Script-only resolution mode leaves the wider capture problem open
refuted.failure_scenario: After this commit, a later design for extension function bodies or SECURITY DEFINER code chooses a different trust rule. Postgres then has two rules for which objects name lookup may see, tied to two different global states. Extension authors have to learn both, and the first rule cannot be removed without breaking scripts.
refuted.argument: Message #1 says function bodies called after install need a different mechanism, so this patch is one context-specific special case. It also fixes an ownership-based trust predicate inside core name resolution. Earlier search_path hardening confined to one context stalled for a similar reason: [P3] was withdrawn partly because it fixed maintenance commands but not other contexts. That reason is an AI summary of the thread, so it is only a pointer.
refuted.author_must_show: How would the trust rule chosen here carry over to extension function bodies and SECURITY DEFINER calls without a second, incompatible rule?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on a future design that nobody has proposed, and message #1 states the script-only scope and its reason. The existing defenses 7eeb1d9861b and b9b21acc766 are also script-only, and P3 was withdrawn on its author's own doubt, so it does not support this.

refuted.title: Existing extension updates can start failing, with no backpatch path
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension script references an object owned by an ordinary role that is not listed in its requires, for example a superuser = false extension's table used for optional integration. After the server upgrade, ALTER EXTENSION ... UPDATE fails as if that object did not exist, and the user learns this during the upgrade window.
refuted.argument: Message #1 accepts this behavior change and calls it rare, but gives no survey of contrib or third-party extensions. A security fix of this kind would normally be considered for back branches. A change that breaks working update scripts cannot go into a minor release, so hosted platforms on supported branches stay exposed. The proposal does not give an escape hatch for scripts that hit the new rule.
refuted.author_must_show: Which known extensions reference objects outside their requires list owned by ordinary roles, and is this meant for back branches or only for master?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which covers the broken update, the missing survey, the missing escape hatch and the back-branch question. Supported branches staying exposed is the current state, so the proposal does not cause it.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The trust rule reads pg_depend, and 0002 touches namespace.c and pg_operator.c; no catalog change is described.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: 0002 changes namespace.h, parse_type.h, plancache.h and extension.h, which extensions include.

touch_points.label: planner behaviour change
touch_points.reason: CachedPlanSource records whether a plan was analyzed inside an extension script, which affects plan reuse.

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The patch adds an ownership-based trust rule to stop privilege escalation through planted objects in extension scripts.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The commit message carries Reported-by for a security issue, but the change can break existing extension scripts.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Each relation, type, function and operator lookup path and each cache must apply the trust check from now on.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The check sits in name lookup and plancache code; the cost outside extension scripts is not measured.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How does the trust rule stop an ordinary role that owns a required extension from adding its own objects with ALTER EXTENSION ... ADD and having them trusted?
What makes a new or changed name-lookup path fail loudly, in tests or by construction, when it skips the trust check during an extension script?
Which contrib or third-party extension scripts reference objects owned by ordinary roles outside their requires list, and how does a user unblock a failed update?
Why does trust stop at direct requires entries, and where would the docs tell extension authors about this new meaning of requires?
Is this meant for back branches or only for master, given that it can make existing update scripts fail?

committability.owner_note: Someone who knows namespace.c, parser name resolution and plancache, and who is willing to sign for a security guarantee about extension scripts.
committability.liability: A documented guarantee that extension scripts never resolve to untrusted objects, kept complete across every current and future lookup path and cache, with no end date. Any missed path becomes a security report.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted v2 in message #7 to cover schema-qualified relation and type names, which shows follow-up during review.

priority.reason: Hosted platforms that run extension scripts as superuser benefit, and two reviewers reproduced the capture. The 83.5 KB patch changes namespace.c, the parser and plancache, and no committer has replied in the visible thread.

provisional_note: The cost of the trust check and the pg_depend lookup, the completeness of the filtered lookup paths, and the plancache handling could not be judged without the code. The answer on ALTER EXTENSION ... ADD may also depend on details of the membership test.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prevent extension creation in temporary schemas
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch first made create extension fail when the target schema is a temporary schema, as alter extension set schema already does. After objections, the author dropped that and changed psql's \dx and \dx+ to hide extensions in other sessions' temporary schemas.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Chris Travers objected that other objects such as types can already be created in temporary schemas, so blocking extensions only would add another special case. The author dropped the block and kept only the \dx and \dx+ fix, which Chris Travers marked Ready for Committer. The author then found that a second session cannot create an extension already created in another session's temporary schema, but \dx no longer lists it. He returned the patch because it does not solve the root problem and makes things more confusing.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch as it stands does not actually solve the root problem and
makes things a bit confusing, so I am marking it as returned with
feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add checks on search_path for IMMUTABLE and SECURITY DEFINER functions
precedents_retrieved.summary: Greg Stark proposed checks at function creation that warn or error when an IMMUTABLE or SECURITY DEFINER function has no search_path set, so that pg_restore failures and index corruption caused by search_path dependence are avoided. A later version instead filled in search_path in proconfig for the user, and he also floated a LEXICAL option modelled on SQL-standard function bodies.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stayed a work in progress: it failed the regression tests, and the author raised open issues himself, namely cache flushes from a per-function search_path and the loss of inlining for functions with proconfig set. Andres Freund noted in October that it did not pass tests and asked whether the author planned further work and whether the entry wanted review. No reply from the author is shown.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This currently obviously doesn't pass tests - are you planning to work on this
further?  As is I'm not really clear what the CF entry is for.

precedents_retrieved.title: Fix search_path for maintenance commands
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch sets search_path to "pg_catalog, pg_temp" while ANALYZE, CLUSTER, REFRESH MATERIALIZED VIEW, REINDEX, VACUUM and CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW run as the table owner. This makes the commands behave the same for every caller and keeps a role with the MAINTAIN privilege from using search_path to gain the table owner's privileges.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Jeff Davis withdrew the patch after a reviewer reported that it no longer applied to HEAD, saying it was not yet clear this was the right change. He had already noted that it forces search_path in maintenance commands but not in other contexts, and that his broader proposals to fix search_path for functions got little agreement. Earlier concerns about breaking functions that depend on search_path were raised in messages not shown. Nathan Bossart supported committing it.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: I am withdrawing this patch from the CF until it's more clear that this is what we really want to do.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add CREATE SCHEMA ... LIKE support
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds `CREATE SCHEMA <name> LIKE <source_schema>` with `INCLUDING | EXCLUDING` options, which copies the objects of a source schema into a new schema. The first version covered tables and indexes; later versions added foreign keys and partitions, with warnings when an object references another schema.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Álvaro Herrera questioned adding DDL syntax for this at all, given the many hard cases and the extra clauses proposed for CREATE SCHEMA. He suggested building on the DDL-generating functions proposed in other threads. The author agreed that a function such as pg_get_schema_ddl() seemed a better way. The visible messages do not show a later version or an explicit closing decision.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This whole thing seems like a giant can of worms, and I'm not sure it's
a good idea to add DDL syntax for it.

precedents_retrieved.title: Tab completion for CREATE SCHEMA AUTHORIZATION
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds psql tab completion for create schema authorization and for the words after create schema <name>. Later versions also complete CURRENT_ROLE, CURRENT_USER and SESSION_USER for other commands that take a role, and merge the duplicated role list queries.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author did not post a new version after review comments in August 2021, so Michael Paquier marked the entry returned with feedback in December. The open comments asked for comments on each role list query and for completion after create schema authorization <role>. Reviewers also pointed out that the patch offered SESSION_USER for create user mapping, where the syntax does not list it, and left out USER.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch has been waiting on author for more than a couple of weeks,
so I have marked it as returned with feedback in the CF app.

precedents_retrieved.title: Support % wildcard in extension upgrade scripts
precedents_retrieved.summary: Let an extension ship an update script with % as the old version, such as postgis--%--3.2.0.sql, which matches any installed version when no explicit update path exists. Later versions made this opt-in with a wildcard_upgrades switch in the .control file.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The last patch failed the extension regression test and no rebase followed, so Daniel Gustafsson marked it returned with feedback. Robert Haas said the real problem was no consensus on a design, since Tom Lane opposed any design that solves the authors' problem. Quoted text from Tom Lane says a wildcard script makes authors promise correct behaviour from any old version, including downgrades, which authors will not do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The fact that consensus is that far away and no patch that applies exist seems to me to indicate that a new CF entry is a better option than pushing forward.

precedents_retrieved.title: Allow excluding pg_temp or pg_catalog from search_path.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds special search_path entries "!pg_temp" and "!pg_catalog" that stop Postgres from searching pg_temp or pg_catalog implicitly, as a safety option for functions. It also warns when a user creates a schema with one of these special names, such as "$user".
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author doubted the feature's value without his separate SEARCH clause proposal, which did not gain support, because users would have to type "!pg_temp" by hand and pg_temp is already ignored for function and operator lookup. The reviewer agreed it was not worth adding without that main use case, and the author withdrew the entry. Earlier review comments also noted that the names need quoting and that "!pg_temp" is ignored when pg_temp is listed explicitly.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I thought it sounded generally useful, but if we're not going to proceed
with the primary use-case for this feature, then perhaps it's not worth
going through this particular one-way door at this time.

precedents_retrieved.title: allow building trusted languages without the untrusted versions
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Tom Lane, Peter Eisentraut, Stephen Frost
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an optional argument to the --with-perl and --with-tcl configure options so a build can include only the trusted or only the untrusted version of PL/Perl and PL/Tcl. For PL/Perl it first splits the trusted and untrusted handler and validator functions, and it adjusts contrib Makefiles that depend on PL/Perl.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane argued that leaving out untrusted languages gives no real security gain, because a user who can create untrusted extensions can already reach the file system through COPY TO PROGRAM. Other reviewers agreed the patch does not by itself let anyone disallow file system access, as the first message claimed. Peter Eisentraut noted that packagers can already choose which files to install. The author said he would withdraw it, and the entry was closed as Returned with feedback.
matched_queries: ignore objects owned by untrusted roles
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Someone who's gained the ability to issue CREATE
EXTENSION on untrusted extensions has already got all the privileges he
needs; leaving out a few extension files is at most going to slow him

precedents_retrieved.title: Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Strip Windows newlines from extension script files manually.
Reverted commit(s): Read extension script files in text not binary mode.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Revert commit 924e03917 in favor of adding code to convert \r\n to \n
explicitly, on Windows only.  The idea of letting text mode do the
work fails for a couple of reasons:

* Per Microsoft documentation, text mode also causes control-Z to be
interpreted as end-of-file.  While it may be unlikely that extension
scripts contain control-Z, we've historically allowed it, and breaking
the case doesn't seem wise.

* Apparently, on some Windows configurations, "r" mode is interpreted
as binary not text mode.  We could force it with "rt" but that would
be inconsistent with our code elsewhere, and it would still require
Windows-specific coding.

Thanks to Alexander Lakhin for investigation.

precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit 98fc31d6499163a0a781aa6f13582a07f09cd7c6.
That change allowed DROP OWNED BY to drop grants of the target
role to other roles, arguing that nobody would need those
privileges anymore.  But that's not so: if you're not superuser,
you still need admin privilege on the target role so you can
drop it.

It's not clear whether or how the dependency-based approach
to solving the original problem can be adapted to keep these
grants.  Since v18 release is fast approaching, the sanest
thing to do seems to be to revert this patch for now.  The
race-condition problem is low severity and not worth taking
risks for.

I didn't force a catversion bump in 98fc31d64, so I won't do
so here either.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent records a reason that applies here. P3, P9 and P11 deal with search_path escalation in maintenance commands: P9 was reverted for timing in the release cycle, P11 records no reason, and P3 was withdrawn without a firm objection. P2 and P7 are different ideas. Message #1 cites the owned-schema proposal and the sandboxing thread but reports no rejection of this approach.
The SQL surface is unchanged: no new syntax, keywords, GUCs or catalog objects. pg_dump and pg_upgrade are not affected by the design as described.

The proposal changes name lookup only while an extension script runs; it adds no on-disk format, WAL record, catalog column or wire protocol message. Plan cache and parallel worker state stay in memory, so I found no persistent or cross-node state to object to; any ABI or backpatch effect of the header changes cannot be judged without the code.
Two objections raised. The error hint naming an ignored candidate tells the script runner only about an object the planting role already knows, so it does not leak information.

Hot-path cost for non-users looks small from the prose, since the checks apply only while creating_extension is set. The size of the plancache flag cost and the pg_depend lookups could not be checked without code or numbers.

No existing feature covers this. Revoking CREATE on the target schema fails when the planting role is the non-superuser installing a trusted extension. Schema-qualifying names and adding casts depends on third-party script authors, and the owned-schema proposal is uncommitted and opt-in. No extension or hook can filter core name lookup.

Demand is real for a security fix: a named external reporter, a hazard the docs already warn about, and two reviewers who reproduced the capture. Cost falls only on extension scripts, and hosted platforms that run scripts as superuser are a large group.
